---
rhema: 1
title: A Constitution of Reason
---

## The problem stated

Reason, the essay argues, is not a faculty but an institution — and institutions have constitutions. The claim is developed in three stages, each corresponding to a failure mode of public argument \[@habermas1984].

## The calculus of assent

If assent were private, convergence would be impossible. Formally, let the assent relation be $A(x, y)$; the essay's contention is that $A$ is transitive only inside a constituted public:

$$
A(x, y) \wedge A(y, z) \Rightarrow A(x, z) \quad \text{iff } x, y, z \in P
$$

where $P$ is the public the constitution defines[^2].

## Objections

The standard objection — that $P$ is circular — is answered in two moves. The first concedes the circularity and relocates it: a constitution defines its own jurisdiction. The second, longer move argues the circularity is virtuous, since every public reasons with the tools the public already shares.

[^2]: The notation is expository; no formalism does argumentative work here.
